Method of Attack: Petya attempts to gain administrative privileges to modify the master boot record (MBR); if unsuccessful, the installer installs Mischa Ransomware instead
Mischa Ransomware encrypts files using AES encryption, appends a 4-character extension, stores the encrypted decryption key at the end of the file, and creates ransom notes with payment instructions
Attack Vector: Email with link to cloud storage containing a disguised executable (PDFBewerbungsmappe.exe)
User execution of the disguised executable
Indicators of Compromise: Executable named PDFBewerbungsmappe.exe with PDF icon
Ransom notes named YOUR_FILES_ARE_ENCRYPTED.HTML and YOUR_FILES_ARE_ENCRYPTED.TXT
Encrypted files with appended 4-character extensions (e.g., test.jpg.7GP3)
TOR payment site with ransom payment wizard
Ransom payment demand of approximately 1.93 bitcoins (~$875 USD)
